chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, all from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever pleases a believer, he has pleased me, and whoever pleases me, he has pleased Allah.'

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir, peace be upon him)
key_terms.سَرَّ: To please / to gladden / to bring joy to

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for pleasing a believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith articulates the Shia concept of 'Tawassul' through spiritual affinity, where pleasing a believer is not merely social kindness but a direct means of attaining divine pleasure. It underscores the elevated status of the 'Momineen' as the beloved of the Prophet and Allah, framing acts of joy-induction as a profound form of worship that bridges the human and divine realms.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, altogether from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Abu Hamza Al Sumaly who said,
‘I heard Abu Ja’farasws saying: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘The one who pleases a Momin so he has pleased measws, and the one who pleases mesaww, so he has pleased Allahazwj’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa all from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from abu Hamza al-Thumali who has said the following: “
I heard abu Ja’far (a.s.) saying, ‘The messenger of Allah has said, “Whoever pleases a believer has pleased me, and whoever, pleases me has pleased Allah.’”
